# AI Teammate — thin stub over the factory home (dmtools-agentic-workflows),
# SELF-HOSTED ENGINE: this repo IS the dmtools-agents engine, so factory_ref
# rides the triggering commit — the factory always executes the exact tree
# under development.
#
# ALL logic lives in IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/
# factory-teammate.yml (guard, legs, verdict, sessions, memory). This file
# carries the repository event triggers + the call only.
#
# Gate: the loop starts when a human ASSIGNS an issue to `ai-teammate`.
# Secrets via `secrets: inherit`: SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN (present), plus
# ZAI_CODE_KEY / KIMI_REVIEW_KEY when the fa/zai runners are used.
#
# gh-676 (2026-10-03): while this file was unparseable (#669 residue —
# duplicate permission keys, fixed in #671), GitHub kept a stale push-event
# registration: every machine-sm state-publish push to `factory-data`
# spawned an instant-fail event=push run with zero jobs ("the phantom").
# This comment block is the standard cure — a no-op touch of the file: the
# default-branch blob change forces GitHub to re-index the registration
# from the real triggers below. There is NO push trigger by design; the
# trigger set (issues + workflow_dispatch only) and the duplicate-key
# ban are guarded by js/unit-tests/test_workflowLint.js.
name: AI Teammate

run-name: "teammate: ${{ github.event_name }} #${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue }} ${{ github.event.inputs.leg }}"

on:
  issues:
    types: [assigned, labeled]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      issue:
        description: 'Issue number (for dispatch runs)'
        type: string
      leg:
        description: 'Which leg to run'
        type: choice
        options: [dev, review, rework]
      reason:
        description: 'Why (audit trail)'
        type: string
      pr:
        description: 'PR number for PR-anchored runs (review leg on PRs born without an issue, #687)'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''

permissions:
  # The factory (factory-teammate.yml@e611e5f) requests this set and a
  # reusable workflow cannot RAISE rights above its caller — the stub must
  # grant the ceiling or every dispatch startup-fails (live dmtools-agents
  # 2026-10-03: 'requesting actions: write, contents: write, issues: write,
  # pull-requests: write, but is only allowed contents: read' — the issue-
  # driven dev lane never ran in this repo).
  actions: write
  contents: write
  issues: write
  pull-requests: write

concurrency:
  group: ai-teammate-${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  teammate:
    # gh-1029: the `labeled` trigger fires on EVERY label write — including
    # the leg's own lifecycle labels (status:*, ai_developed, ...) — and
    # `on:` cannot filter by label name. The old assignee-only clause
    # admitted any labeled event on an assigned issue, so each leg
    # re-triggered a guaranteed no-op run that parked in the same
    # concurrency group (live: run 39111715487 → 39111765329 on #1027,
    # 2026-10-18). The gate therefore keys the action: `assigned` requires
    # the ai-teammate assignee; `labeled` proceeds ONLY for the arming
    # labels — lifecycle labels never allocate a runner.
    if: >-
      github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' ||
      (github.event_name == 'issues' &&
       github.event.action == 'assigned' &&
       contains(github.event.issue.assignees.*.login, 'ai-teammate')) ||
      (github.event_name == 'issues' &&
       github.event.action == 'labeled' &&
       (github.event.label.name == 'agent:dev' ||
        github.event.label.name == 'agent:develop' ||
        github.event.label.name == 'agent:review' ||
        github.event.label.name == 'agent:rework' ||
        github.event.label.name == 'pr_approved'))
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-teammate.yml@main
    with:
      issue: ${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue }}
      pr: ${{ github.event.inputs.pr || '' }}
      machine-author: 'ai-teammate'
      leg: ${{ github.event.inputs.leg || '' }}
      reason: ${{ github.event.inputs.reason || github.event_name }}
      flutter-version: ''  # JS/configs repo — dmtools & fa CLIs are prebuilt; no Flutter toolchain needed
      # 2026-10-17 incident: GitHub's ubuntu-slim SKU started force-cancelling
      # teammate jobs at exactly ~15m24s (6/6 legs tonight, 15:20–15:26;
      # "The operation was canceled" from the control plane, conclusion=cancelled).
      # Yesterday the same SKU ran legs for 24 min fine. dmtools-dart legs on
      # ubuntu-24.04 are unaffected. Owner decision: CI checks stay on slim,
      # ai-teammate legs move to ubuntu-latest until slim is healthy again.
      runner: 'ubuntu-latest'
    secrets: inherit

How does the probe distinguish "the run that this very event started"? When an assigned+labeled double event fires, two workflow runs get queued nearly simultaneously. Both start the probe job. Run 1 probes: no active run → proceed. Run 2 probes: run 1 is active → skip. That's the desired outcome. But there's a race: both probe before either's "teammate" job starts. The probe lists runs of workflow ai-teammate.yml in the repo with status queued/in_progress. Both probe jobs are themselves runs of ai-teammate.yml! So run 2 sees run 1 (queued/in_progress) → skip. Design for gh-1065:

**Pure module**: `js/common/teammateEventDedup.js` — decides, for an issues-event run, whether to proceed or skip, given:
- the current run's id/number (to break the tie: only older active runs suppress us)
- the list of runs of ai-teammate.yml (with status, conclusion, created_at/updated_at, run id/number, and the issue anchor — how do we key by issue?)

Keying by issue: the concurrency group is `ai-teammate-<issue>`. The REST API `listWorkflowRuns` response doesn't include the concurrency group, but includes `head_branch` (for issues events, head_branch is the default branch since it's an issues event... actually issues events run on the default branch). Hmm. How to tell which issue a run belongs to? The run-name! run-name: `teammate: ${{ github.event_name }} #${ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue }} ${{ github.event.inputs.leg }}`. The API returns `name` (run-name) and also `display_title`. So we can match by run-name containing `#<issue>` anchor token. But wait — the SM dispatch run-name in the template is `▶ {leg} (SM) · gh-{issue}` format. In this repo's stub, run-name is `teammate: workflow_dispatch #N leg`. Both carry the issue number as `#N` or `gh-N`.

Hmm, but is name-matching robust? The gh-715/944 title guards in smAgent match title anchor tokens. Let me check how smAgent's title guards key the issue. Let me look at hasActiveTargetWorkflowRun / the title matching code.

Also AC2: "same issue + same leg". Leg in run-name: `teammate: issues #1040 ` (empty leg for issues events) vs dispatch: `teammate: workflow_dispatch #1040 dev`. The event-path run doesn't know its leg in advance... The labeled arming labels map to legs (agent:dev → dev, agent:review → review, etc.). Actually the factory derives leg from labels. For the dedup key, we could use issue + leg where leg is derived from the event (assigned → unknown leg → dedup on any leg? ; labeled agent:dev → dev).

# Quality gate — per-function CRAP ratchet via crap4js (IstiN fork).

# Quality gate — per-function CRAP ratchet via crap4js (IstiN fork).
#
# Policy: CRAP may only DECREASE. The baseline (per-function CRAP of everything above
# CRAP_THRESHOLD) is NOT in the repository — with many agents opening PRs a committed file
# conflicts constantly. It lives in a rolling GitHub release asset:
#
#   release tag  crap-baseline   (prerelease, never "latest" — agent pack consumers resolve
#                                 releases/latest, so this one must not be it)
#   asset        crap-baseline.json
#
# pull_request / workflow_dispatch (the factory SM dispatches this on PR heads): measure the
#   head and COMPARE with the released baseline. Fails when a function's CRAP grew or a new
#   function exceeds CRAP_THRESHOLD; labels crap:regression / crap:improved.
# main (push, merge-bot completion via workflow_run — the bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, which
#   never fires 'push' —, or manual dispatch on main): after a green measurement, ratchet the
#   released baseline DOWN (crap4js --update-baseline: min(old, now), never up, refuses on
#   regression) and upload it. The release notes carry 'main@<sha>' so repeated triggers for
#   the same HEAD are skipped. Concurrent merges are serialized by the concurrency group.
# No baseline asset yet (first run / fork): bootstrap from the measured main, no comparison.
#
# Coverage comes from the unit suite run in the same job (instrumented tree), so the
# ratchet is evaluated with the unit-test results of the head.
#
# Tool pin: IstiN/crap4js by commit SHA (fork of vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit/crap4js v0.15.0 +
# --baseline / --update-baseline, pipe-safe exit). Installed from GitHub — the npm 'crap4js'
# package is an unrelated third-party project.
name: Quality

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_run:
    # The merge bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, and GitHub suppresses workflow triggers on
    # GITHUB_TOKEN events — the push trigger above never fires for machine merges (same
    # reason agent-pack-release.yml listens to this workflow, gh-867). The bot's own run
    # completion is a normal event. Runs on every bot completion are cheap no-ops: the
    # 'gate' job skips when the baseline already covers main's HEAD.
    workflows: ['Machine Merge Bot']
    types: [completed]
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:  # the Machine SM / sm-kicker dispatch validation runs; on main it re-seeds the baseline

permissions:
  contents: write        # push to main: update the crap-baseline release asset
  pull-requests: write   # crap:regression / crap:improved labels

# Serializes baseline updates of consecutive merges (never cancels a running update).
concurrency:
  group: quality-${{ (github.event_name == 'push' || github.event_name == 'workflow_run' || github.ref == 'refs/heads/main') && 'baseline-update' || github.run_id }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

env:
  # Threshold for functions NOT in crap-baseline.json (new or renamed code).
  CRAP_THRESHOLD: '8'
  CRAP4JS_REPO: 'IstiN/crap4js'
  CRAP4JS_REF: '83ee6201e554a91d51c298f045c5c4cb47317b6d'
  BASELINE_TAG: 'crap-baseline'
  BASELINE_ASSET: 'crap-baseline.json'

jobs:
  gate:
    # PR / dispatch on a PR head: always measure. Main-side events (push, merge-bot completion,
    # manual dispatch on main): measure only when the released baseline does not yet cover HEAD.
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    outputs:
      run: ${{ steps.g.outputs.run }}
    steps:
      - id: g
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          EVENT: ${{ github.event_name }}
          REF: ${{ github.ref }}
          BOT_CONCLUSION: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.conclusion }}
        run: |
          main_side=false
          [ "$EVENT" = "push" ] || [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && main_side=true
          [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_dispatch" ] && [ "$REF" = "refs/heads/main" ] && main_side=true
          if [ "$main_side" != "true" ]; then
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; exit 0      # pull_request / dispatch on a PR head: always measure
          fi

# SM kicker — thin stub over the canonical watchdog in the factory home.
# All logic (sm-liveness + head-completeness) lives in
# IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-sm-kicker.yml.
# This repo's validation CI is `Quality` (display name "Quality") and its
# required context is the `crap` job.
name: SM kicker

run-name: '🥁 kicker ${{ github.event_name }} ${{ github.ref_name }}'

on:
  push:
    branches-ignore: [main]
  schedule:
    - cron: '13,43 * * * *'
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  actions: write
  contents: read
  pull-requests: read
  checks: read

concurrency:
  # dmtools-agents#682 (live fa#1202/#1203 2026-10-03, still reproducing
  # 2026-10-04 06:21–06:22 in THIS repo — runs 06:36/06:41/06:43): the
  # global group below already ran with cancel-in-progress:false, yet
  # kicker runs kept dying cancelled in chains. cancel-in-progress only
  # shields the RUNNING run — a queued run in the same group ALWAYS
  # supersedes (cancels) the pending one (GitHub docs: "Any existing
  # pending job or workflow in the same concurrency group, if it exists,
  # will be canceled and the new queued job or workflow will take its
  # place"). One global group meant every push anywhere (silent refresh,
  # factory-data snapshots, dev waves) cancelled every other branch's
  # pending kicker. Per-head-SHA group: no push can displace another
  # push's kicker — a queued kicker that is about to dispatch a tick
  # always gets to run (canonical fix + consumer notes: IstiN/
  # dmtools-agentic-workflows factory-sm-kicker.yml). Effective once the
  # canonical pin is bumped (separate PR): until then the called
  # workflow's own global group still supersedes.
  group: sm-kicker-${{ github.sha }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  kicker:
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-sm-kicker.yml@main
    with:
      sm_workflow: machine-sm.yml
      ci_workflow: quality.yml
      ci_display_name: Quality
      required_contexts: crap

# AI Teammate — GitHub-issues machine runner (TEMPLATE).
#
# Copy into the TARGET repository (.github/workflows/ai-teammate.yml) and
# adapt the RUNNER_* entries. This is the trimmed generic variant of the
# battle-tested machine-kit workflow (see epam/dmtools-dart
# .github/workflows/ai-teammate.yml for the full reference with comments).
#
# Two entry paths, and BOTH must survive for the loop to be self-healing:
#   1. issues: [assigned, labeled] — the fast path (labels added with a
#      real PAT fire events; GITHUB_TOKEN-added labels do NOT — that is
#      exactly what the SM cron covers)
#   2. workflow_dispatch (issue / leg / reason) — the SM dispatch path:
#      the reconciler fires this directly, so mute labels cannot stall the
#      loop
#
# The guard derives the leg: dispatch input leg > label agent:rework >
# label agent:review > assignee/agent:dev (dev). Each leg runs the dmtools
# agent config named by RUNNER_*: dev (story/bug) develops from the issue
# body, review produces a machine PR review verdict, rework fixes the
# linked PR by the review threads.
name: 'AI Teammate'

# Run title carries the EFFECTIVE anchor (owner 2026-09-27, live: dmd run
# 36333172145): a PR-anchored SM dispatch (#544/#687 — inputs.pr set,
# inputs.issue empty) must title '▶ rework (SM) · pr-266', never the
# malformed '▶ rework (SM) · gh- · gh-: '. (inputs.pr || '') guards the
# label-event path, where inputs are null — null != '' would be TRUE and
# render 'pr-' for ordinary issue events.
run-name: >-
  ${{ github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' &&
      format('▶ {0} (SM) · {1}', github.event.inputs.leg,
        (github.event.inputs.pr || '') != '' && format('pr-{0}', github.event.inputs.pr)
        || format('gh-{0}', github.event.inputs.issue)) ||
      github.event.label.name == 'agent:rework' && '🔧 rework' ||
      github.event.label.name == 'agent:review' && '🔍 review' ||
      '⚒️ dev' }}
  · ${{ (github.event.inputs.pr || '') != '' && format('pr-{0}', github.event.inputs.pr)
      || format('gh-{0}', github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue) }}${{
      github.event.issue.title && format(': {0}', github.event.issue.title) || '' }}

on:
  issues:
    types: [assigned, labeled]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      issue:
        description: 'Issue number to run the agent on (empty for PR-anchored runs, #687)'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''
      leg:
        description: 'Which leg to run'
        required: true
        type: choice
        options: [dev, review, rework]
      reason:
        description: 'Why this dispatch (audit trail, shown in logs)'
        required: false
        type: string
      pr:
        description: 'PR number for PR-anchored runs (#544/#687) — the SM dispatches review/rework with pr instead of issue when the PR has no resolvable LOCAL issue'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''

concurrency:
  # PR-anchored dispatches (#544/#687) carry no issue — fall back to the pr
  # input so each PR keeps its OWN group ('ai-teammate-issue-pr-266');
  # without it every PR-anchored run shares the empty group and serializes
  # across unrelated PRs.
  group: ai-teammate-issue-${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue || format('pr-{0}', github.event.inputs.pr) }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

permissions:
  contents: write
  pull-requests: write
  issues: write
  actions: write

env:
  AGENT_HANDLE: ai-teammate
  # ── adapt per target repo ───────────────────────────────────────────────
  RUNNER_STORY: dmtools-agents/story_development.json
  RUNNER_BUG: dmtools-agents/bug_development.json
  RUNNER_REVIEW: dmtools-agents/pr_review.json
  RUNNER_REWORK: dmtools-agents/pr_rework.json
  DMTOOLS_AGENTS_REF: main
  DMTOOLS_VERSION: v0.1.5
  FA_VERSION: latest
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Secrets expected: SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN (PAT), plus the AI provider key
  # referenced by the runner configs (e.g. ZAI_CODE_KEY / KIMI_REVIEW_KEY).

jobs:
  guard:
    # gh-1029: the `labeled` trigger fires on EVERY label write — including
    # the leg's own lifecycle labels (status:*, ai_developed, ...) — and
    # `on:` cannot filter by label name. Without this job-level gate the
    # guard allocated a runner on each lifecycle-label write only to decide
    # run=false (the self-retrigger no-op burn). `assigned` and the arming
    # `labeled` events (agent:*) still enter; lifecycle labels skip the job
    # entirely and never allocate a runner.
    if: >-
      github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' ||
      (github.event_name == 'issues' &&
       github.event.action == 'assigned') ||
      (github.event_name == 'issues' &&
       github.event.action == 'labeled' &&
       (github.event.label.name == 'agent:dev' ||
        github.event.label.name == 'agent:develop' ||
        github.event.label.name == 'agent:review' ||
        github.event.label.name == 'agent:rework' ||
        github.event.label.name == 'pr_approved'))
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    outputs:
      run: ${{ steps.check.outputs.run }}
      runner: ${{ steps.check.outputs.runner }}
      kind: ${{ steps.check.outputs.kind }}
    steps:
      - name: Decide whether this event is for the agent
        id: check
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          NUMBER: ${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue }}

{"content":"# gh-1065 — Root Cause Analysis

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: Assigning an issue (or assigning while labels change) starts TWO (observed: up to THREE on #1061) `ai-teammate.yml` runs per issue — one per event in the burst — and the owner cancels the duplicates by hand.

**Root cause**: `.github/workflows/ai-teammate.yml` triggers on `issues: [assigned, labeled]` AND the SM tick dispatches the same legs via `workflow_dispatch`. One human action emits multiple events (`assigned` + one `labeled` per label write), and each event unconditionally starts its own run. Neither path checks whether a run for the same issue/leg is already in flight: the gh-1028 dedup (`js/common/branchLegGuard.js` + `smAgent.triggerWorkflow`) guards the SM-internal dispatch path only — the GitHub-event path bypasses that ledger entirely. The per-issue `concurrency:` group (`cancel-in-progress: false`) only SERIALIZES the duplicates (queued no-op burns); it never drops them.

**Impact**: Every assign/label burst on an issue assigned to `ai-teammate` allocates duplicate runners (token waste ×2–3 per action), parks no-op runs in the concurrency queue, and forces the owner to hand-cancel duplicates (live 2026-10-18: #1040–#1043 two runs each at 20:11Z, #1061 three runs across 20:07–20:15).

**Fix approach**: Add an event-path dedup gate to the workflow stub, keyed exactly like the gh-1028 SM-side dedup (same issue + same leg + in-flight or freshly-completed run ⇒ skip), with a deterministic tie-break (only an OLDER run suppresses, so exactly one run of a same-second burst survives) and fail-open probe errors (AC3 — a broken probe must never swallow the only trigger). The decision logic is a pure, unit-tested module `js/common/teammateEventDedup.js` (same pattern as `branchLegGuard.js`); the workflow wires it via a `dedup` job that probes the repo's `ai-teammate.yml` runs through the per-status fan-out and gates the `teammate` reusable-workflow call on `needs.dedup.outputs.proceed`.

**Previous attempt**: none — fresh bug (gh-1028 fixed the SM-dispatch side only; the event side was out of its scope).

# AI Teammate — thin stub over the factory home (dmtools-agentic-workflows),
# SELF-HOSTED ENGINE: this repo IS the dmtools-agents engine, so factory_ref
# rides the triggering commit — the factory always executes the exact tree
# under development.
#
# ALL logic lives in IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/
# factory-teammate.yml (guard, legs, verdict, sessions, memory). This file
# carries the repository event triggers + the call only.
#
# Gate: the loop starts when a human ASSIGNS an issue to `ai-teammate`.
# Secrets via `secrets: inherit`: SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN (present), plus
# ZAI_CODE_KEY / KIMI_REVIEW_KEY when the fa/zai runners are used.
#
# gh-676 (2026-10-03): while this file was unparseable (#669 residue —
# duplicate permission keys, fixed in #671), GitHub kept a stale push-event
# registration: every machine-sm state-publish push to `factory-data`
# spawned an instant-fail event=push run with zero jobs ("the phantom").
# This comment block is the standard cure — a no-op touch of the file: the
# default-branch blob change forces GitHub to re-index the registration
# from the real triggers below. There is NO push trigger by design; the
# trigger set (issues + workflow_dispatch only) and the duplicate-key
# ban are guarded by js/unit-tests/test_workflowLint.js.
name: AI Teammate

run-name: "teammate: ${{ github.event_name }} #${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue }} ${{ github.event.inputs.leg }}"

on:
  issues:
    types: [assigned, labeled]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      issue:
        description: 'Issue number (for dispatch runs)'
        type: string
      leg:
        description: 'Which leg to run'
        type: choice
        options: [dev, review, rework]
      reason:
        description: 'Why (audit trail)'
        type: string
      pr:
        description: 'PR number for PR-anchored runs (review leg on PRs born without an issue, #687)'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''

permissions:
  # The factory (factory-teammate.yml@e611e5f) requests this set and a
  # reusable workflow cannot RAISE rights above its caller — the stub must
  # grant the ceiling or every dispatch startup-fails (live dmtools-agents
  # 2026-10-03: 'requesting actions: write, contents: write, issues: write,
  # pull-requests: write, but is only allowed contents: read' — the issue-
  # driven dev lane never ran in this repo).
  actions: write
  contents: write
  issues: write
  pull-requests: write

concurrency:
  group: ai-teammate-${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  teammate:
    # gh-1029: the `labeled` trigger fires on EVERY label write — including
    # the leg's own lifecycle labels (status:*, ai_developed, ...) — and
    # `on:` cannot filter by label name. The old assignee-only clause
    # admitted any labeled event on an assigned issue, so each leg
    # re-triggered a guaranteed no-op run that parked in the same
    # concurrency group (live: run 39111715487 → 39111765329 on #1027,
    # 2026-10-18). The gate therefore keys the action: `assigned` requires
    # the ai-teammate assignee; `labeled` proceeds ONLY for the arming
    # labels — lifecycle labels never allocate a runner.
    if: >-
      github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' ||
      (github.event_name == 'issues' &&
       github.event.action == 'assigned' &&
       contains(github.event.issue.assignees.*.login, 'ai-teammate')) ||
      (github.event_name == 'issues' &&
       github.event.action == 'labeled' &&
       (github.event.label.name == 'agent:dev' ||
        github.event.label.name == 'agent:develop' ||
        github.event.label.name == 'agent:review' ||
        github.event.label.name == 'agent:rework' ||
        github.event.label.name == 'pr_approved'))
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-teammate.yml@main
    with:
      issue: ${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue }}
      pr: ${{ github.event.inputs.pr || '' }}
      machine-author: 'ai-teammate'
      leg: ${{ github.event.inputs.leg || '' }}
      reason: ${{ github.event.inputs.reason || github.event_name }}
      flutter-version: ''  # JS/configs repo — dmtools & fa CLIs are prebuilt; no Flutter toolchain needed
      # 2026-10-17 incident: GitHub's ubuntu-slim SKU started force-cancelling
      # teammate jobs at exactly ~15m24s (6/6 legs tonight, 15:20–15:26;
      # "The operation was canceled" from the control plane, conclusion=cancelled).
      # Yesterday the same SKU ran legs for 24 min fine. dmtools-dart legs on
      # ubuntu-24.04 are unaffected. Owner decision: CI checks stay on slim,
      # ai-teammate legs move to ubuntu-latest until slim is healthy again.
      runner: 'ubuntu-latest'
    secrets: inherit

# Quality gate — per-function CRAP ratchet via crap4js (IstiN fork).
#
# Policy: CRAP may only DECREASE. The baseline (per-function CRAP of everything above
# CRAP_THRESHOLD) is NOT in the repository — with many agents opening PRs a committed file
# conflicts constantly. It lives in a rolling GitHub release asset:
#
#   release tag  crap-baseline   (prerelease, never "latest" — agent pack consumers resolve
#                                 releases/latest, so this one must not be it)
#   asset        crap-baseline.json
#
# pull_request / workflow_dispatch (the factory SM dispatches this on PR heads): measure the
#   head and COMPARE with the released baseline. Fails when a function's CRAP grew or a new
#   function exceeds CRAP_THRESHOLD; labels crap:regression / crap:improved.
# main (push, merge-bot completion via workflow_run — the bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, which
#   never fires 'push' —, or manual dispatch on main): after a green measurement, ratchet the
#   released baseline DOWN (crap4js --update-baseline: min(old, now), never up, refuses on
#   regression) and upload it. The release notes carry 'main@<sha>' so repeated triggers for
#   the same HEAD are skipped. Concurrent merges are serialized by the concurrency group.
# No baseline asset yet (first run / fork): bootstrap from the measured main, no comparison.
#
# Coverage comes from the unit suite run in the same job (instrumented tree), so the
# ratchet is evaluated with the unit-test results of the head.
#
# Tool pin: IstiN/crap4js by commit SHA (fork of vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit/crap4js v0.15.0 +
# --baseline / --update-baseline, pipe-safe exit). Installed from GitHub — the npm 'crap4js'
# package is an unrelated third-party project.
name: Quality

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_run:
    # The merge bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, and GitHub suppresses workflow triggers on
    # GITHUB_TOKEN events — the push trigger above never fires for machine merges (same
    # reason agent-pack-release.yml listens to this workflow, gh-867). The bot's own run
    # completion is a normal event. Runs on every bot completion are cheap no-ops: the
    # 'gate' job skips when the baseline already covers main's HEAD.
    workflows: ['Machine Merge Bot']
    types: [completed]
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:  # the Machine SM / sm-kicker dispatch validation runs; on main it re-seeds the baseline

permissions:
  contents: write        # push to main: update the crap-baseline release asset
  pull-requests: write   # crap:regression / crap:improved labels

# Serializes baseline updates of consecutive merges (never cancels a running update).
concurrency:
  group: quality-${{ (github.event_name == 'push' || github.event_name == 'workflow_run' || github.ref == 'refs/heads/main') && 'baseline-update' || github.run_id }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

env:
  # Threshold for functions NOT in crap-baseline.json (new or renamed code).
  CRAP_THRESHOLD: '8'
  CRAP4JS_REPO: 'IstiN/crap4js'
  CRAP4JS_REF: '83ee6201e554a91d51c298f045c5c4cb47317b6d'
  BASELINE_TAG: 'crap-baseline'
  BASELINE_ASSET: 'crap-baseline.json'

jobs:
  gate:
    # PR / dispatch on a PR head: always measure. Main-side events (push, merge-bot completion,
    # manual dispatch on main): measure only when the released baseline does not yet cover HEAD.
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    outputs:
      run: ${{ steps.g.outputs.run }}
    steps:
      - id: g
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          EVENT: ${{ github.event_name }}
          REF: ${{ github.ref }}
          BOT_CONCLUSION: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.conclusion }}
        run: |
          main_side=false
          [ "$EVENT" = "push" ] || [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && main_side=true
          [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_dispatch" ] && [ "$REF" = "refs/heads/main" ] && main_side=true
          if [ "$main_side" != "true" ]; then
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; exit 0      # pull_request / dispatch on a PR head: always measure
          fi

# All logic (sm-liveness + head-completeness) lives in
# IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-sm-kicker.yml.

  schedule:

# AI Teammate — GitHub-issues machine runner (TEMPLATE).
#
# Copy into the TARGET repository (.github/workflows/ai-teammate.yml) and
# adapt the RUNNER_* entries. This is the trimmed generic variant of the
# battle-tested machine-kit workflow (see epam/dmtools-dart
# .github/workflows/ai-teammate.yml for the full reference with comments).
#
# Two entry paths, and BOTH must survive for the loop to be self-healing:
#   1. issues: [assigned, labeled] — the fast path (labels added with a
#      real PAT fire events; GITHUB_TOKEN-added labels do NOT — that is
#      exactly what the SM cron covers)
#   2. workflow_dispatch (issue / leg / reason) — the SM dispatch path:
#      the reconciler fires this directly, so mute labels cannot stall the
#      loop
#
# The guard derives the leg: dispatch input leg > label agent:rework >
# label agent:review > assignee/agent:dev (dev). Each leg runs the dmtools
# agent config named by RUNNER_*: dev (story/bug) develops from the issue
# body, review produces a machine PR review verdict, rework fixes the
# linked PR by the review threads.
name: 'AI Teammate'

# Run title carries the EFFECTIVE anchor (owner 2026-09-27, live: dmd run
# 36333172145): a PR-anchored SM dispatch (#544/#687 — inputs.pr set,
# inputs.issue empty) must title '▶ rework (SM) · pr-266', never the
# malformed '▶ rework (SM) · gh- · gh-: '. (inputs.pr || '') guards the
# label-event path, where inputs are null — null != '' would be TRUE and
# render 'pr-' for ordinary issue events.
run-name: >-
  ${{ github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' &&
      format('▶ {0} (SM) · {1}', github.event.inputs.leg,
        (github.event.inputs.pr || '') != '' && format('pr-{0}', github.event.inputs.pr)
        || format('gh-{0}', github.event.inputs.issue)) ||
      github.event.label.name == 'agent:rework' && '🔧 rework' ||
      github.event.label.name == 'agent:review' && '🔍 review' ||
      '⚒️ dev' }}
  · ${{ (github.event.inputs.pr || '') != '' && format('pr-{0}', github.event.inputs.pr)
      || format('gh-{0}', github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue) }}${{
      github.event.issue.title && format(': {0}', github.event.issue.title) || '' }}

on:
  issues:
    types: [assigned, labeled]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      issue:
        description: 'Issue number to run the agent on (empty for PR-anchored runs, #687)'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''
      leg:
        description: 'Which leg to run'
        required: true
        type: choice
        options: [dev, review, rework]
      reason:
        description: 'Why this dispatch (audit trail, shown in logs)'
        required: false
        type: string
      pr:
        description: 'PR number for PR-anchored runs (#544/#687) — the SM dispatches review/rework with pr instead of issue when the PR has no resolvable LOCAL issue'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''

concurrency:
  # PR-anchored dispatches (#544/#687) carry no issue — fall back to the pr
  # input so each PR keeps its OWN group ('ai-teammate-issue-pr-266');
  # without it every PR-anchored run shares the empty group and serializes
  # across unrelated PRs.
  group: ai-teammate-issue-${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue || format('pr-{0}', github.event.inputs.pr) }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

permissions:
  contents: write
  pull-requests: write
  issues: write
  actions: write

env:
  AGENT_HANDLE: ai-teammate
  # ── adapt per target repo ───────────────────────────────────────────────
  RUNNER_STORY: dmtools-agents/story_development.json
  RUNNER_BUG: dmtools-agents/bug_development.json
  RUNNER_REVIEW: dmtools-agents/pr_review.json
  RUNNER_REWORK: dmtools-agents/pr_rework.json
  DMTOOLS_AGENTS_REF: main
  DMTOOLS_VERSION: v0.1.5
  FA_VERSION: latest
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Secrets expected: SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN (PAT), plus the AI provider key
  # referenced by the runner configs (e.g. ZAI_CODE_KEY / KIMI_REVIEW_KEY).

jobs:
  guard:
    # gh-1029: the `labeled` trigger fires on EVERY label write — including
    # the leg's own lifecycle labels (status:*, ai_developed, ...) — and
    # `on:` cannot filter by label name. Without this job-level gate the
    # guard allocated a runner on each lifecycle-label write only to decide
    # run=false (the self-retrigger no-op burn). `assigned` and the arming
    # `labeled` events (agent:*) still enter; lifecycle labels skip the job
    # entirely and never allocate a runner.
    if: >-
      github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' ||
      (github.event_name == 'issues' &&
       github.event.action == 'assigned') ||
      (github.event_name == 'issues' &&
       github.event.action == 'labeled' &&
       (github.event.label.name == 'agent:dev' ||
        github.event.label.name == 'agent:develop' ||
        github.event.label.name == 'agent:review' ||
        github.event.label.name == 'agent:rework' ||
        github.event.label.name == 'pr_approved'))
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    outputs:
      run: ${{ steps.check.outputs.run }}
      runner: ${{ steps.check.outputs.runner }}
      kind: ${{ steps.check.outputs.kind }}
    steps:
      - name: Decide whether this event is for the agent
        id: check
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          NUMBER: ${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue }}
          ASSIGNEES: ${{ join(github.event.issue.assignees.*.login, ' ') }}
          LABELS: ${{ join(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, ' ') }}
          INPUT_LEG: ${{ github.event.inputs.leg }}
        run: |
          if [ -n "$INPUT_LEG" ]; then
            LABELS="$(gh issue view "$NUMBER" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json labels -q '[.labels[].name] | join(" ")')"
            ASSIGNEES="$(gh issue view "$NUMBER" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json assignees -q '[.assignees[].login] | join(" ")')"
          fi
          state="$(gh issue view "$NUMBER" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json state -q .state)"
          if [ "$state" != "OPEN" ]; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; exit 0
          fi
          if echo "$LABELS" | grep -qw "agent:skip"; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; exit 0
          fi
          runner=""
          if [ "$INPUT_LEG" = "rework" ]; then runner="$RUNNER_REWORK";
          elif [ "$INPUT_LEG" = "review" ]; then runner="$RUNNER_REVIEW";
          elif [ "$INPUT_LEG" = "dev" ]; then
            title="$(gh issue view "$NUMBER" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json title -q .title)"
            if echo "$title" | grep -qiE '^\[?bug\]' || echo "$LABELS" | grep -qwi "bug"; then
              runner="$RUNNER_BUG"
            else
              runner="$RUNNER_STORY"
            fi
          elif echo "$LABELS" | grep -qw "agent:rework"; then runner="$RUNNER_REWORK";
          elif echo "$LABELS" | grep -qw "agent:review"; then runner="$RUNNER_REVIEW";
          elif echo "$ASSIGNEES" | grep -qw "$AGENT_HANDLE" || echo "$LABELS" | grep -qw "agent:dev"; then
            title="$(gh issue view "$NUMBER" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json title -q .title)"
            if echo "$title" | grep -qiE '^\[?bug\]' || echo "$LABELS" | grep -qwi "bug"; then
              runner="$RUNNER_BUG"
            else
              runner="$RUNNER_STORY"
            fi
          fi
          if [ -n "$runner" ]; then
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "runner=$runner" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "kind=$(echo "$runner" | grep -q review && echo review || (echo "$runner" | grep -q rework && echo rework || echo dev))" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          else
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

  teammate:
    needs: guard
    if: needs.guard.outputs.run == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 60
    steps:
      # Adapt the runner steps from the machine-kit reference workflow:
      # checkout (target + dmtools-agents), install dmtools + fa, write the
      # issue body to input/ticket.md, then:
      #   dmtools run "$RUNNER" '{"params":{"ticketKey":"gh-<n>"}}'
      # Fu…

{"content":"# gh-1065 — Root Cause Analysis

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: Assigning an issue (or assigning while labels change) starts TWO (observed: up to THREE on #1061) `ai-teammate.yml` runs per issue — one per event in the burst — and the owner cancels the duplicates by hand.

**Root cause**: `.github/workflows/ai-teammate.yml` triggers on `issues: [assigned, labeled]` AND the SM tick dispatches the same legs via `workflow_dispatch`. One human action emits multiple events (`assigned` + one `labeled` per label write), and each event unconditionally starts its own run. Neither path checks whether a run for the same issue/leg is already in flight: the gh-1028 dedup (`js/common/branchLegGuard.js` + `smAgent.triggerWorkflow`) guards the SM-internal dispatch path only — the GitHub-event path bypasses that ledger entirely. The per-issue `concurrency:` group (`cancel-in-progress: false`) only SERIALIZES the duplicates (queued no-op burns); it never drops them.

**Impact**: Every assign/label burst on an issue assigned to `ai-teammate` allocates duplicate runners (token waste ×2–3 per action), parks no-op runs in the concurrency queue, and forces the owner to hand-cancel duplicates (live 2026-10-18: #1040–#1043 two runs each at 20:11Z, #1061 three runs across 20:07–20:15).

**Fix approach**: Add an event-path dedup gate to the workflow stub, keyed exactly like the gh-1028 SM-side dedup (same issue + same leg + in-flight or freshly-completed run ⇒ skip), with a deterministic tie-break (only an OLDER run suppresses, so exactly one run of a same-second burst survives) and fail-open probe errors (AC3 — a broken probe must never swallow the only trigger). The decision logic is a pure, unit-tested module `js/common/teammateEventDedup.js` (same pattern as `branchLegGuard.js`); the workflow wires it via a `dedup` job that probes the repo's `ai-teammate.yml` runs through the per-status fan-out and gates the `teammate` reusable-workflow call on `needs.dedup.outputs.proceed`.

**Previous attempt**: none — fresh bug (gh-1028 fixed the SM-dispatch side only; the event side was out of its scope).

# AI Teammate — thin stub over the factory home (dmtools-agentic-workflows),
# SELF-HOSTED ENGINE: this repo IS the dmtools-agents engine, so factory_ref
# rides the triggering commit — the factory always executes the exact tree
# under development.
#
# ALL logic lives in IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/
# factory-teammate.yml (guard, legs, verdict, sessions, memory). This file
# carries the repository event triggers + the call only.
#
# Gate: the loop starts when a human ASSIGNS an issue to `ai-teammate`.
# Secrets via `secrets: inherit`: SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN (present), plus
# ZAI_CODE_KEY / KIMI_REVIEW_KEY when the fa/zai runners are used.
#
# gh-676 (2026-10-03): while this file was unparseable (#669 residue —
# duplicate permission keys, fixed in #671), GitHub kept a stale push-event
# registration: every machine-sm state-publish push to `factory-data`
# spawned an instant-fail event=push run with zero jobs ("the phantom").
# This comment block is the standard cure — a no-op touch of the file: the
# default-branch blob change forces GitHub to re-index the registration
# from the real triggers below. There is NO push trigger by design; the
# trigger set (issues + workflow_dispatch only) and the duplicate-key
# ban are guarded by js/unit-tests/test_workflowLint.js.
name: AI Teammate

run-name: "teammate: ${{ github.event_name }} #${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue }} ${{ github.event.inputs.leg }}"

on:
  issues:
    types: [assigned, labeled]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      issue:
        description: 'Issue number (for dispatch runs)'
        type: string
      leg:
        description: 'Which leg to run'
        type: choice
        options: [dev, review, rework]
      reason:
        description: 'Why (audit trail)'
        type: string
      pr:
        description: 'PR number for PR-anchored runs (review leg on PRs born without an issue, #687)'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''

permissions:
  # The factory (factory-teammate.yml@e611e5f) requests this set and a
  # reusable workflow cannot RAISE rights above its caller — the stub must
  # grant the ceiling or every dispatch startup-fails (live dmtools-agents
  # 2026-10-03: 'requesting actions: write, contents: write, issues: write,
  # pull-requests: write, but is only allowed contents: read' — the issue-
  # driven dev lane never ran in this repo).
  actions: write
  contents: write
  issues: write
  pull-requests: write

concurrency:
  group: ai-teammate-${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  teammate:
    # gh-1029: the `labeled` trigger fires on EVERY label write — including
    # the leg's own lifecycle labels (status:*, ai_developed, ...) — and
    # `on:` cannot filter by label name. The old assignee-only clause
    # admitted any labeled event on an assigned issue, so each leg
    # re-triggered a guaranteed no-op run that parked in the same
    # concurrency group (live: run 39111715487 → 39111765329 on #1027,
    # 2026-10-18). The gate therefore keys the action: `assigned` requires
    # the ai-teammate assignee; `labeled` proceeds ONLY for the arming
    # labels — lifecycle labels never allocate a runner.
    if: >-
      github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' ||
      (github.event_name == 'issues' &&
       github.event.action == 'assigned' &&
       contains(github.event.issue.assignees.*.login, 'ai-teammate')) ||
      (github.event_name == 'issues' &&
       github.event.action == 'labeled' &&
       (github.event.label.name == 'agent:dev' ||
        github.event.label.name == 'agent:develop' ||
        github.event.label.name == 'agent:review' ||
        github.event.label.name == 'agent:rework' ||
        github.event.label.name == 'pr_approved'))
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-teammate.yml@main
    with:
      issue: ${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue }}
      pr: ${{ github.event.inputs.pr || '' }}
      machine-author: 'ai-teammate'
      leg: ${{ github.event.inputs.leg || '' }}
      reason: ${{ github.event.inputs.reason || github.event_name }}
      flutter-version: ''  # JS/configs repo — dmtools & fa CLIs are prebuilt; no Flutter toolchain needed
      # 2026-10-17 incident: GitHub's ubuntu-slim SKU started force-cancelling
      # teammate jobs at exactly ~15m24s (6/6 legs tonight, 15:20–15:26;
      # "The operation was canceled" from the control plane, conclusion=cancelled).
      # Yesterday the same SKU ran legs for 24 min fine. dmtools-dart legs on
      # ubuntu-24.04 are unaffected. Owner decision: CI checks stay on slim,
      # ai-teammate legs move to ubuntu-latest until slim is healthy again.
      runner: 'ubuntu-latest'
    secrets: inherit

Keying: "same issue + same leg". The run-name carries leg info? For issues events, leg is not inputs. Hmm, the event path doesn't know the leg in advance — leg is derived in factory-teammate.yml. But AC1 says "exactly ONE teammate run per issue per leg". The concurrency group is `ai-teammate-<issue>`. For the event path, the leg is deduced from labels (agent:dev → dev, etc.) — but the labeled gate admits arming labels. Actually the dedup can be at issue level: if any ai-teammate run for this issue is active or freshly completed, drop the duplicate trigger. That satisfies "one run per issue per leg" conservatively.

How does the probe distinguish "the run that this very event started"? When an assigned+labeled double event fires, two workflow runs get queued nearly simultaneously. Both start the probe job. Run 1 probes: no active run → proceed. Run 2 probes: run 1 is active → skip. That's the desired outcome. But there's a race: both probe before either's "teammate" job starts. The probe lists runs of workflow ai-teammate.yml in the repo with status queued/in_progress. Both probe jobs are themselves runs of ai-teammate.yml! So run 2 sees run 1 (queued/in_progress) → skip. That breaks AC3/AC1 ("must not silently swallow the only trigger").

To break the tie, we need ordering: e.g., compare run creation time — only skip if the other run was created BEFORE this run (run_number < this run's). Since run numbers are monotonic in a repo, the probe can compare `databaseId`/`run_number` of active runs vs `github.run_id`/`github.run_number`. Skip only if another active run for the same issue has run_number < ours. That ensures the earliest run proceeds. That's a classic dedup.

Design for gh-1065:

**Pure module**: `js/common/teammateEventDedup.js` — decides, for an issues-event run, whether to proceed or skip, given:
- the current run's id/number (to break the tie: only older active runs suppress us)
- the list of runs of ai-teammate.yml (with status, conclusion, created_at/updated_at, run id/number, and the issue anchor — how do we key by issue?)

Keying by issue: the concurrency group is `ai-teammate-<issue>`. The REST API `listWorkflowRuns` response doesn't include the concurrency group, but includes `head_branch` (for issues events, head_branch is the default branch since it's an issues event... actually issues events run on the default branch). Hmm. How to tell which issue a run belongs to? The run-name! run-name: `teammate: ${{ github.event_name }} #${ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue }} ${{ github.event.inputs.leg }}`. The API returns `name` (run-name) and also `display_title`. So we can match by run-name containing `#<issue>` anchor token. But wait — the SM dispatch run-name in the template is `▶ {leg} (SM) · gh-{issue}` format. In this repo's stub, run-name is `teammate: workflow_dispatch #N leg`. Both carry the issue number as `#N` or `gh-N`.

Hmm, but is name-matching robust? The gh-715/944 title guards in smAgent match title anchor tokens. Let me check how smAgent's title guards key the issue. Let me look at hasActiveTargetWorkflowRun / the title matching code.

Also AC2: "same issue + same leg". Leg in run-name: `teammate: issues #1040 ` (empty leg for issues events) vs dispatch: `teammate: workflow_dispatch #1040 dev`. The event-path run doesn't know its leg in advance... The labeled arming labels map to legs (agent:dev → dev, agent:review → review, etc.). Actually the factory derives leg from labels. For the dedup key, we could use issue + leg where leg is derived from the event (assigned → unknown leg → dedup on any leg? ; labeled agent:dev → dev).

Hmm, this is getting complicated. Let me simplify per AC1: "exactly ONE teammate run per issue per leg" — and AC2: "same issue + same leg + in-flight or freshly-completed ⇒ skip". A conservative implementation: skip if any ai-teammate run for the same issue is active (excluding self, only older runs) or freshly completed. Since all legs for an issue funnel through one issue-keyed concurrency group, issue-level dedup gives per-leg dedup too.

Wait, but must be careful: the SM dispatch path also runs ai-teammate.yml (workflow_dispatch). Now the leg part: the concurrency group is `ai-teammate-<issue>` — per-issue, not per-leg. So GitHub-level, one issue = one group. How to determine the event's leg in the stub? From the event payload:

So dedup key = issue + leg(derived) suffices for AC1.

Given the complexity, a pragmatic and defensible design (v1, per ticket title):

**Event-path dedup keyed on issue + leg**, where leg is derived in the stub:
- `labeled` event → leg from the arming label: agent:dev/agent:develop → dev, agent:review/pr_approved → review, agent:rework → rework.

# Quality gate — per-function CRAP ratchet via crap4js (IstiN fork).
#
# Policy: CRAP may only DECREASE. The baseline (per-function CRAP of everything above
# CRAP_THRESHOLD) is NOT in the repository …

blocks.text:
# Quality gate — per-function CRAP ratchet via crap4js (IstiN fork).
#
# Policy: CRAP may only DECREASE. The baseline (per-function CRAP of everything above
# CRAP_THRESHOLD) is NOT in the repository — with many agents opening PRs a committed file
# conflicts constantly. It lives in a rolling GitHub release asset:
#
#   release tag  crap-baseline   (prerelease, never "latest" — agent pack consumers resolve
#                                 releases/latest, so this one must not be it)
#   asset        crap-baseline.json
#
# pull_request / workflow_dispatch (the factory SM dispatches this on PR heads): measure the
#   head and COMPARE with the released baseline. Fails when a function's CRAP grew or a new
#   function exceeds CRAP_THRESHOLD; labels crap:regression / crap:improved.
# main (push, merge-bot completion via workflow_run — the bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, which
#   never fires 'push' —, or manual dispatch on main): after a green measurement, ratchet the
#   released baseline DOWN (crap4js --update-baseline: min(old, now), never up, refuses on
#   regression) and upload it. The release notes carry 'main@<sha>' so repeated triggers for
#   the same HEAD are skipped. Concurrent merges are serialized by the concurrency group.
# No baseline asset yet (first run / fork): bootstrap from the measured main, no comparison.
#
# Coverage comes from the unit suite run in the same job (instrumented tree), so the
# ratchet is evaluated with the unit-test results of the head.
#
# Tool pin: IstiN/crap4js by commit SHA (fork of vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit/crap4js v0.15.0 +
# --baseline / --update-baseline, pipe-safe exit). Installed from GitHub — the npm 'crap4js'
# package is an unrelated third-party project.
name: Quality

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_run:
    # The merge bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, and GitHub suppresses workflow triggers on
    # GITHUB_TOKEN events — the push trigger above never fires for machine merges (same
    # reason agent-pack-release.yml listens to this workflow, gh-867). The bot's own run
    # completion is a normal event. Runs on every bot completion are cheap no-ops: the
    # 'gate' job skips when the baseline already covers main's HEAD.
    workflows: ['Machine Merge Bot']
    types: [completed]
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:  # the Machine SM / sm-kicker dispatch validation runs; on main it re-seeds the baseline

permissions:
  contents: write        # push to main: update the crap-baseline release asset
  pull-requests: write   # crap:regression / crap:improved labels

# Serializes baseline updates of consecutive merges (never cancels a running update).
concurrency:
  group: quality-${{ (github.event_name == 'push' || github.event_name == 'workflow_run' || github.ref == 'refs/heads/main') && 'baseline-update' || github.run_id }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

env:
  # Threshold for functions NOT in crap-baseline.json (new or renamed code).
  CRAP_THRESHOLD: '8'
  CRAP4JS_REPO: 'IstiN/crap4js'
  CRAP4JS_REF: '83ee6201e554a91d51c298f045c5c4cb47317b6d'
  BASELINE_TAG: 'crap-baseline'
  BASELINE_ASSET: 'crap-baseline.json'

jobs:
  gate:
    # PR / dispatch on a PR head: always measure. Main-side events (push, merge-bot completion,
    # manual dispatch on main): measure only when the released baseline does not yet cover HEAD.
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    outputs:
      run: ${{ steps.g.outputs.run }}
    steps:
      - id: g
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          EVENT: ${{ github.event_name }}
          REF: ${{ github.ref }}
          BOT_CONCLUSION: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.conclusion }}
        run: |
          main_side=false
          [ "$EVENT" = "push" ] || [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && main_side=true
          [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_dispatch" ] && [ "$REF" = "refs/heads/main" ] && main_side=true
          if [ "$main_side" != "true" ]; then
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; exit 0      # pull_request / dispatch on a PR head: always measure
          fi
====
# SM kicker — thin stub over the canonical watchdog in the factory home.
# All logic (sm-liveness + head-completeness) lives in
# IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-sm-kicker.yml.
# This repo's validation CI is `Quality` (display name "Quality") and its
# required context is the `crap` job.
name: SM kicker

run-name: '🥁 kicker ${{ github.event_name }} ${{ github.ref_name }}'

on:
  push:
    branches-ignore: [main]
  schedule:
    - cron: '13,43 * * * *'
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  actions: write
  contents: read
  pull-requests: read
  checks: read

concurrency:
  # dmtools-agents#682 (live fa#1202/#1203 2026-10-03, still reproducing
  # 2026-10-04 06:21–06:22 in THIS repo — runs 06:36/06:41/06:43): the
  # global group below already ran with cancel-in-progress:false, yet
  # kicker runs kept dying cancelled in chains. cancel-in-progress only
  # shields the RUNNING run — a queued run in the same group ALWAYS
  # supersedes (cancels) the pending one (GitHub docs: "Any existing
  # pending job or workflow in the same concurrency group, if it exists,
  # will be canceled and the new queued job or workflow will take its
  # place"). One global group meant every push anywhere (silent refresh,
  # factory-data snapshots, dev waves) cancelled every other branch's
  # pending kicker. Per-head-SHA group: no push can displace another
  # push's kicker — a queued kicker that is about to dispatch a tick
  # always gets to run (canonical fix + consumer notes: IstiN/
  # dmtools-agentic-workflows factory-sm-kicker.yml). Effective once the
  # canonical pin is bumped (separate PR): until then the called
  # workflow's own global group still supersedes.
  group: sm-kicker-${{ github.sha }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  kicker:
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-sm-kicker.yml@main
    with:
      sm_workflow: machine-sm.yml
      ci_workflow: quality.yml
      ci_display_name: Quality
      required_contexts: crap

# AI Teammate — GitHub-issues machine runner (TEMPLATE).
#
# Copy into the TARGET repository (.github/workflows/ai-teammate.yml) and
# adapt the RUNNER_* entries. This is the trimmed generic variant of the
# battle-tested machine-kit workflow (see epam/dmtools-dart
# .github/workflows/ai-teammate.yml for the full reference with comments).
#
# Two entry paths, and BOTH must survive for the loop to be self-healing:
#   1. issues: [assigned, labeled] — the fast path (labels added with a
#      real PAT fire events; GITHUB_TOKEN-added labels do NOT — that is
#      exactly what the SM cron covers)
#   2. workflow_dispatch (issue / leg / reason) — the SM dispatch path:
#      the reconciler fires this directly, so mute labels cannot stall the
#      loop
#
# The guard derives the leg: dispatch input leg > label agent:rework >
# label agent:review > assignee/agent:dev (dev). Each leg runs the dmtools
# agent config named by RUNNER_*: dev (story/bug) develops from the issue
# body, review produces a machine PR review verdict, rework fixes the
# linked PR by the review threads.
name: 'AI Teammate'

# Run title carries the EFFECTIVE anchor (owner 2026-09-27, live: dmd run
# 36333172145): a PR-anchored SM dispatch (#544/#687 — inputs.pr set,
# inputs.issue empty) must title '▶ rework (SM) · pr-266', never the
# malformed '▶ rework (SM) · gh- · gh-: '. (inputs.pr || '') guards the
# label-event path, where inputs are null — null != '' would be TRUE and
# render 'pr-' for ordinary issue events.
run-name: >-
  ${{ github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' &&
      format('▶ {0} (SM) · {1}', github.event.inputs.leg,
        (github.event.inputs.pr || '') != '' && format('pr-{0}', github.event.inputs.pr)
        || format('gh-{0}', github.event.inputs.issue)) ||
      github.event.label.name == 'agent:rework' && '🔧 rework' ||
      github.event.label.name == 'agent:review' && '🔍 review' ||
      '⚒️ dev' }}
  · ${{ (github.event.inputs.pr || '') != '' && format('pr-{0}', github.event.inputs.pr)
      || format('gh-{0}', github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue) }}${{
      github.event.issue.title && format(': {0}', github.event.issue.title) || '' }}

on:
  issues:
    types: [assigned, labeled]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      issue:
        description: 'Issue number to run the agent on (empty for PR-anchored runs, #687)'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''
      leg:
        description: 'Which leg to run'
        required: true
        type: choice
        options: [dev, review, rework]
      reason:
        description: 'Why this dispatch (audit trail, shown in logs)'
        required: false
        type: string
      pr:
        description: 'PR number for PR-anchored runs (#544/#687) — the SM dispatches review/rework with pr instead of issue when the PR has no resolvable LOCAL issue'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''

concurrency:
  # PR-anchored dispatches (#544/#687) carry no issue — fall back to the pr
  # input so each PR keeps its OWN group ('ai-teammate-issue-pr-266');
  # without it every PR-anchored run shares the empty group and serializes
  # across unrelated PRs.
  group: ai-teammate-issue-${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue || format('pr-{0}', github.event.inputs.pr) }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

permissions:
  contents: write
  pull-requests: write
  issues: write
  actions: write

env:
  AGENT_HANDLE: ai-teammate
  # ── adapt per target repo ───────────────────────────────────────────────
  RUNNER_STORY: dmtools-agents/story_development.json
  RUNNER_BUG: dmtools-agents/bug_development.json
  RUNNER_REVIEW: dmtools-agents/pr_review.json
  RUNNER_REWORK: dmtools-agents/pr_rework.json
  DMTOOLS_AGENTS_REF: main
  DMTOOLS_VERSION: v0.1.5
  FA_VERSION: latest
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Secrets expected: SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN (PAT), plus the AI provider key
  # referenced by the runner configs (e.g. ZAI_CODE_KEY / KIMI_REVIEW_KEY).

jobs:
  guard:
    # gh-1029: the `labeled` trigger fires on EVERY label write — including
    # the leg's own lifecycle labels (status:*, ai_developed, ...) — and
    # `on:` cannot filter by label name. Without this job-level gate the
    # guard allocated a runner on each lifecycle-label write only to decide
    # run=false (the self-retrigger no-op burn). `assigned` and the arming
    # `labeled` events (agent:*) still enter; lifecycle labels skip the job
    # entirely and never allocate a runner.
    if: >-
      github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' ||
      (github.event_name == 'issues' &&
       github.event.action == 'assigned') ||
      (github.event_name == 'issues' &&
       github.event.action == 'labeled' &&
       (github.event.label.name == 'agent:dev' ||
        github.event.label.name == 'agent:develop' ||
        github.event.label.name == 'agent:review' ||
        github.event.label.name == 'agent:rework' ||
        github.event.label.name == 'pr_approved'))
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    outputs:
      run: ${{ steps.check.outputs.run }}
      runner: ${{ steps.check.outputs.runner }}
      kind: ${{ steps.check.outputs.kind }}
    steps:
      - name: Decide whether this event is for the agent
        id: check
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          NUMBER: ${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue }}
          ASSIGNEES: ${{ join(github.event.issue.assignees.*.login, ' ') }}
          LABELS: ${{ join(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, ' ') }}
          INPUT_LEG: ${{ github.event.inputs.leg }}
        run: |
          if [ -n "$INPUT_LEG" ]; then
            LABELS="$(gh issue view "$NUMBER" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json labels -q '[.labels[].name] | join(" ")')"
            ASSIGNEES="$(gh issue view "$NUMBER" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json assignees -q '[.assignees[].login] | join(" ")')"
          fi
          state="$(gh issue view "$NUMBER" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json state -q .state)"
          if [ "$state" != "OPEN" ]; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; exit 0
          fi
          if echo "$LABELS" | grep -qw "agent:skip"; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; exit 0
          fi
          runner=""
          if [ "$INPUT_LEG" = "rework" ]; then runner="$RUNNER_REWORK";
          elif [ "$INPUT_LEG" = "review" ]; then runner="$RUNNER_REVIEW";
          elif [ "$INPUT_LEG" = "dev" ]; then
            title="$(gh issue view "$NUMBER" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json title -q .title)"
            if echo "$title" | grep -qiE '^\[?bug\]' || echo "$LABELS" | grep -qwi "bug"; then
              runner="$RUNNER_BUG"
            else
              runner="$RUNNER_STORY"
            fi
          elif echo "$LABELS" | grep -qw "agent:rework"; then runner="$RUNNER_REWORK";
          elif echo "$LABELS" | grep -qw "agent:review"; then runner="$RUNNER_REVIEW";
          elif echo "$ASSIGNEES" | grep -qw "$AGENT_HANDLE" || echo "$LABELS" | grep -qw "agent:dev"; then
            title="$(gh issue view "$NUMBER" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json title -q .title)"
            if echo "$title" | grep -qiE '^\[?bug\]' || echo "$LABELS" | grep -qwi "bug"; then
              runner="$RUNNER_BUG"
            else
              runner="$RUNNER_STORY"
            fi
          fi
          if [ -n "$runner" ]; then
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "runner=$runner" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "kind=$(echo "$runner" | grep -q review && echo review || (echo "$runner" | grep -q rework && echo rework || echo dev))" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          else
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

  teammate:
    needs: guard
    if: needs.guard.outputs.run == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 60
    steps:
      # Adapt the runner steps from the machine-kit reference workflow:
      # checkout (target + dmtools-agents), install dmtools + fa, write the
      # issue body to input/ticket.md, then:
      #   dmtools run "$RUNNER" '{"params":{"ticketKey":"gh-<n>"}}'
      # Fu…

{"content":"# gh-1065 — Root Cause Analysis

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: Assigning an issue (or assigning while labels change) starts TWO (observed: up to THREE on #1061) `ai-teammate.yml` runs per issue — one per event in the burst — and the owner cancels the duplicates by hand.

**Root cause**: `.github/workflows/ai-teammate.yml` triggers on `issues: [assigned, labeled]` AND the SM tick dispatches the same legs via `workflow_dispatch`. One human action emits multiple events (`assigned` + one `labeled` per label write), and each event unconditionally starts its own run. Neither path checks whether a run for the same issue/leg is already in flight: the gh-1028 dedup (`js/common/branchLegGuard.js` + `smAgent.triggerWorkflow`) guards the SM-internal dispatch path only — the GitHub-event path bypasses that ledger entirely. The per-issue `concurrency:` group (`cancel-in-progress: false`) only SERIALIZES the duplicates (queued no-op burns); it never drops them.

**Impact**: Every assign/label burst on an issue assigned to `ai-teammate` allocates duplicate runners (token waste ×2–3 per action), parks no-op runs in the concurrency queue, and forces the owner to hand-cancel duplicates (live 2026-10-18: #1040–#1043 two runs each at 20:11Z, #1061 three runs across 20:07–20:15).

**Fix approach**: Add an event-path dedup gate to the workflow stub, keyed exactly like the gh-1028 SM-side dedup (same issue + same leg + in-flight or freshly-completed run ⇒ skip), with a deterministic tie-break (only an OLDER run suppresses, so exactly one run of a same-second burst survives) and fail-open probe errors (AC3 — a broken probe must never swallow the only trigger). The decision logic is a pure, unit-tested module `js/common/teammateEventDedup.js` (same pattern as `branchLegGuard.js`); the workflow wires it via a `dedup` job that probes the repo's `ai-teammate.yml` runs through the per-status fan-out and gates the `teammate` reusable-workflow call on `needs.dedup.outputs.proceed`.

**Previous attempt**: none — fresh bug (gh-1028 fixed the SM-dispatch side only; the event side was out of its scope).

# AI Teammate — thin stub over the factory home (dmtools-agentic-workflows),
# SELF-HOSTED ENGINE: this repo IS the dmtools-agents engine, so factory_ref
# rides the triggering commit — the factory always executes the exact tree
# under development.
#
# ALL logic lives in IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/
# factory-teammate.yml (guard, legs, verdict, sessions, memory). This file
# carries the repository event triggers + the call only.
#
# Gate: the loop starts when a human ASSIGNS an issue to `ai-teammate`.
# Secrets via `secrets: inherit`: SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN (present), plus
# ZAI_CODE_KEY / KIMI_REVIEW_KEY when the fa/zai runners are used.
#
# gh-676 (2026-10-03): while this file was unparseable (#669 residue —
# duplicate permission keys, fixed in #671), GitHub kept a stale push-event
# registration: every machine-sm state-publish push to `factory-data`
# spawned an instant-fail event=push run with zero jobs ("the phantom").
# This comment block is the standard cure — a no-op touch of the file: the
# default-branch blob change forces GitHub to re-index the registration
# from the real triggers below. There is NO push trigger by design; the
# trigger set (issues + workflow_dispatch only) and the duplicate-key
# ban are guarded by js/unit-tests/test_workflowLint.js.
name: AI Teammate

run-name: "teammate: ${{ github.event_name }} #${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue }} ${{ github.event.inputs.leg }}"

on:
  issues:
    types: [assigned, labeled]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      issue:
        description: 'Issue number (for dispatch runs)'
        type: string
      leg:
        description: 'Which leg to run'
        type: choice
        options: [dev, review, rework]
      reason:
        description: 'Why (audit trail)'
        type: string
      pr:
        description: 'PR number for PR-anchored runs (review leg on PRs born without an issue, #687)'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''

permissions:
  # The factory (factory-teammate.yml@e611e5f) requests this set and a
  # reusable workflow cannot RAISE rights above its caller — the stub must
  # grant the ceiling or every dispatch startup-fails (live dmtools-agents
  # 2026-10-03: 'requesting actions: write, contents: write, issues: write,
  # pull-requests: write, but is only allowed contents: read' — the issue-
  # driven dev lane never ran in this repo).
  actions: write
  contents: write
  issues: write
  pull-requests: write

concurrency:
  group: ai-teammate-${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  teammate:
    # gh-1029: the `labeled` trigger fires on EVERY label write — including
    # the leg's own lifecycle labels (status:*, ai_developed, ...) — and
    # `on:` cannot filter by label name. The old assignee-only clause
    # admitted any labeled event on an assigned issue, so each leg
    # re-triggered a guaranteed no-op run that parked in the same
    # concurrency group (live: run 39111715487 → 39111765329 on #1027,
    # 2026-10-18). The gate therefore keys the action: `assigned` requires
    # the ai-teammate assignee; `labeled` proceeds ONLY for the arming
    # labels — lifecycle labels never allocate a runner.
    if: >-
      github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' ||
      (github.event_name == 'issues' &&
       github.event.action == 'assigned' &&
       contains(github.event.issue.assignees.*.login, 'ai-teammate')) ||
      (github.event_name == 'issues' &&
       github.event.action == 'labeled' &&
       (github.event.label.name == 'agent:dev' ||
        github.event.label.name == 'agent:develop' ||
        github.event.label.name == 'agent:review' ||
        github.event.label.name == 'agent:rework' ||
        github.event.label.name == 'pr_approved'))
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-teammate.yml@main
    with:
      issue: ${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue }}
      pr: ${{ github.event.inputs.pr || '' }}
      machine-author: 'ai-teammate'
      leg: ${{ github.event.inputs.leg || '' }}
      reason: ${{ github.event.inputs.reason || github.event_name }}
      flutter-version: ''  # JS/configs repo — dmtools & fa CLIs are prebuilt; no Flutter toolchain needed
      # 2026-10-17 incident: GitHub's ubuntu-slim SKU started force-cancelling
      # teammate jobs at exactly ~15m24s (6/6 legs tonight, 15:20–15:26;
      # "The operation was canceled" from the control plane, conclusion=cancelled).
      # Yesterday the same SKU ran legs for 24 min fine. dmtools-dart legs on
      # ubuntu-24.04 are unaffected. Owner decision: CI checks stay on slim,
      # ai-teammate legs move to ubuntu-latest until slim is healthy again.
      runner: 'ubuntu-latest'
    secrets: inherit

- For issues events: query GitHub API for active runs of ai-teammate.yml for the same issue (concurrency group `ai-teammate-<N>`), plus recently completed runs (fresh window). If one exists → skip with an audit log line. On API error → fail-open (proceed).

Keying: "same issue + same leg". The run-name carries leg info? For issues events, leg is not inputs. Hmm, the event path doesn't know the leg in advance — leg is derived in factory-teammate.yml. But AC1 says "exactly ONE teammate run per issue per leg". The concurrency group is `ai-teammate-<issue>`. For the event path, the leg is deduced from labels (agent:dev → dev, etc.) — but the labeled gate admits arming labels. Actually the dedup can be at issue level: if any ai-teammate run for this issue is active or freshly completed, drop the duplicate trigger. That satisfies "one run per issue per leg" conservatively.

How does the probe distinguish "the run that this very event started"? When an assigned+labeled double event fires, two workflow runs get queued nearly simultaneously. Both start the probe job. Run 1 probes: no active run → proceed. Run 2 probes: run 1 is active → skip. That's the desired outcome. But there's a race: both probe before either's "teammate" job starts. The probe lists runs of workflow ai-teammate.yml in the repo with status queued/in_progress. Both probe jobs are themselves runs of ai-teammate.yml! So run 2 sees run 1 (queued/in_progress) → skip. And run 1 sees run 2 too, if run 2 was created before run 1's probe executes. Hmm — race: both runs created within milliseconds; both probes may see the other as queued → both skip → zero runs. That breaks AC3/AC1 ("must not silently swallow the only trigger").

To break the tie, we need ordering: e.g., compare run creation time — only skip if the other run was created BEFORE this run (run_number < this run's). Since run numbers are monotonic in a repo, the probe can compare `databaseId`/`run_number` of active runs vs `github.run_id`/`github.run_number`. Skip only if another active run for the same issue has run_number < ours. That ensures the earliest run proceeds. That's a classic dedup.

messages.preview: Let me look at how workflows run JS in this repo and check the quality workflow:

blocks.text:
Now I have a good picture. The established pattern:

1. Pure module in `js/common/` (e.g., `branchLegGuard.js`) with decision logic.
2. Transport half wired in the caller (smAgent for SM-side).
3. Unit tests in `js/unit-tests/test_*.js` + `run_*.json` manifest.
4. The workflow file gets structural lint tests (test_workflowLint.js style) plus template tests.

Design for gh-1065:

**Pure module**: `js/common/teammateEventDedup.js` — decides, for an issues-event run, whether to proceed or skip, given:
- the current run's id/number (to break the tie: only older active runs suppress us)
- the list of runs of ai-teammate.yml (with status, conclusion, created_at/updated_at, run id/number, and the issue anchor — how do we key by issue?)

Keying by issue: the concurrency group is `ai-teammate-<issue>`. The REST API `listWorkflowRuns` response doesn't include the concurrency group, but includes `head_branch` (for issues events, head_branch is the default branch since it's an issues event... actually issues events run on the default branch). Hmm. How to tell which issue a run belongs to? The run-name! run-name: `teammate: ${{ github.event_name }} #${ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue }} ${{ github.event.inputs.leg }}`. The API returns `name` (run-name) and also `display_title`. So we can match by run-name containing `#<issue>` anchor token. But wait — the SM dispatch run-name in the template is `▶ {leg} (SM) · gh-{issue}` format. In this repo's stub, run-name is `teammate: workflow_dispatch #N leg`. Both carry the issue number as `#N` or `gh-N`.

Hmm, but is name-matching robust? The gh-715/944 title guards in smAgent match title anchor tokens. Let me check how smAgent's title guards key the issue. Let me look at hasActiveTargetWorkflowRun / the title matching code.

Also AC2: "same issue + same leg". Leg in run-name: `teammate: issues #1040 ` (empty leg for issues events) vs dispatch: `teammate: workflow_dispatch #1040 dev`. The event-path run doesn't know its leg in advance... The labeled arming labels map to legs (agent:dev → dev, agent:review → review, etc.). Actually the factory derives leg from labels. For the dedup key, we could use issue + leg where leg is derived from the event (assigned → unknown leg → dedup on any leg? ; labeled agent:dev → dev).

Hmm, this is getting complicated. Let me simplify per AC1: "exactly ONE teammate run per issue per leg" — and AC2: "same issue + same leg + in-flight or freshly-completed ⇒ skip". A conservative implementation: skip if any ai-teammate run for the same issue is active (excluding self, only older runs) or freshly completed. Since all legs for an issue funnel through one issue-keyed concurrency group, issue-level dedup gives per-leg dedup too.

Wait, but must be careful: the SM dispatch path also runs ai-teammate.yml (workflow_dispatch). If SM dispatches a leg for issue #1040 (dev), and then a human assigns the issue, the assigned event should be dropped (leg already in flight) — yes! That's exactly the ticket's race: "assigned + labeled + SM dispatch race". So the probe must consider ALL runs of ai-teammate.yml for the same issue regardless of trigger event, including workflow_dispatch runs from the SM.

Now the leg part: the concurrency group is `ai-teammate-<issue>` — per-issue, not per-leg. So GitHub-level, one issue = one group. For the probe: any active run for the issue (older than ours) ⇒ skip. Leg matching: dispatch runs carry `inputs.leg` in run-name (`teammate: workflow_dispatch #1040 dev`); issues events carry empty leg. If the event is a labeled event with arming label agent:review, the actual leg will be review. Should we only skip if an active review-leg run exists? If we skip whenever ANY leg is in flight, we could drop a legitimately different leg trigger (e.g., dev in flight, review label added → review leg should start? But concurrency group would queue it anyway... `cancel-in-progress: false` so it queues and runs after). Hmm — dropping a different-leg trigger would break multi-leg flows. So leg matching matters.

How to determine the event's leg in the stub? From the event payload:
